sources.measured_here: every bounding box was measured by parsing the binary STL on disk

units: millimetres (binary STL carries no unit field; slicers assume mm)
what_this_is_not: The geometry is SCHEMATIC. Organ shapes, sizes and positions are generated from a parameter set, not measured from a specimen.
The one evidence-backed proportion is the pectoral fin: pectoral_len_over_SL and the span and area that follow from it. Everything else is a plausible arrangement.
Cell tokens are MARKERS for recorded cell types, not models of cells. No cell-level geometry exists in the source and none was invented.
The animal is a DESIGN, not a described species. No fish like this has been observed.
Any glide figure attached to this geometry is UNVERIFIED. See the README.

banner.head: This animal is hypothetical.
banner.text: HYPOTHETICAL: this piece belongs to the design 'winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish', not to any described animal. It was generated from a parameter set, not observed.

banner.head: What this kit deliberately abandons.
banner.text: At life size the small viscera (spleen 1.3 mm, heart 2.1 mm, head kidney 1.6 mm, kidney a 0.4 mm thread), the individual vertebrae, the fin rays, the rib struts and the separate girdle bones are all below the 0.50 mm printable wall or the 2.50 mm handleable minimum. They are merged into chunky blocks rather than inflated 10-80x, and every merge is recorded per part. The 120 mm kit keeps them separate.

banner.head: The hierarchy is flattened.
banner.text: FLATTENED: there are no organ-system carriers at 1:1, so every part pegs straight into the body case. The containment hierarchy is NOT expressed by this kit; the 120 mm kit is the one that teaches it.

banner.head: Print the coupon first, then pick the socket.
banner.text: Print the fit-test coupon before anything else: five blind D-sockets at 0.05, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12 and 0.16 mm radial clearance, labelled, with six identical pegs. The tightest socket a peg enters by hand without forcing, and holds without glue, is the clearance to build at. This kit is built at 0.1 mm; if the coupon picks another, rebuild with that number (anatomy-model/print/README.md).

about.title: The SLA values this kit is built on
paras: Every peg and socket has a raised index triangle beside it; align the triangles and the part is the right way round. Nothing needs glue. The two case halves mate on three keyed midline pins.

banner.head: This animal is hypothetical.
banner.text: HYPOTHETICAL: this piece belongs to the design 'winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish', not to any described animal. It was generated from a parameter set, not observed.

banner.head: Organ system → organ → tissue, as physical parts.
banner.text: THE CONTAINMENT-HIERARCHY KIT. Organ systems are top-level carrier trays, each organ seats into its system, and the four tissue-level pieces seat in turn. This is the kit that teaches the hierarchy; the 1:1 starter cannot. Cell tokens would be handleable at this scale, but they are NOT among these 56 files: the 75-cell-type register is carried as data in cell_tokens.registry.

banner.head: 2 parts: do not print without inspecting them.
banner.text: Brain (nervous__brain__organ): volume cross-check failed: surface integral 180.0 mm3 vs Monte Carlo 131.7 mm3 - a shell is probably wound inside out. Head kidney (renal__head-kidney__organ): volume cross-check failed: surface integral 76.4 mm3 vs Monte Carlo 53.8 mm3 - a shell is probably wound inside out. This is the same signature as the sealed-cavity bug recorded in the README.

banner.head: 12 of 56 parts fail a check, and none was dropped.
banner.text: 4 fail a real check (a wall under the 1.2 mm minimum, or not watertight), 6 could not have their wall measured with enough samples to judge, and 2 fail the volume cross-check. Every reason is in the parts list.

120 mm SL, 146.3415 mm per model unit
print/winged-zebrafish-whole-120mm.stl and print/winged-zebrafish-glider-120mm.stl, which are the 0.35-fin winged-zebrafish design

about.title: How the hierarchy is built
rows: 4 pieces: the skin halves, split fore and aft to fit a 200 mm plate
13 trays, generated as printing fixtures (not anatomy); each legs into a case half
35 pieces, each pegged into its system's carrier on a boss of its true anatomical height
paras: Joinery: D-keyed peg into a matching socket, one rotation only, with a raised index triangle beside each. Parent of every part is the manifest field seats_into.
Cell tokens and register cards are designed for this scale but are not among these 56 files; the 75-cell-type register is in the manifest as data.

kits.scale_line: Exported at scale factor 140.7129436712351 with standard length measured to the skin tip (0.8528 model units), not the hypural plate (0.82).

frame.axes: +X anterior (snout), +Y the fish’s left flank, +Z dorsal

banner.head: Superseded.
banner.text: This is the first, fast export of the 100 GLB objects. It is replaced by the 1:1 starter kit and the 120 mm hierarchy kit and will be removed. It has no joinery, no thickening and no verification beyond watertightness.

banner.head: About 3.8% undersized.
banner.text: Measured: the whole-fish file is 4.0% / 4.0% / 3.5% larger in X / Y / Z. Standard length was measured to the posterior skin tip (0.8528 model units) instead of the hypural plate (0.82), so every part is small. Nothing has been rescaled.

banner.head: 11 of the 100 parts will not print.
banner.text: A single-layer sheet with no interior — zero wall thickness — so a slicer has nothing to fill; it needs a solidify/thicken pass (roughly 0.8–1.2 mm) first.

banner.head: Hypothetical, and the fins are a chosen value.
banner.text: The design uses pectoral_len_over_SL = 0.35, an assumed delta; the flying fish's measured median is 0.687 (Daane 2021). a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder (0.155) and the flying-fish measured median (0.687), near the flying-halfbeak median 0.274-0.388 (Daane groups). Chosen, not measured.
